 Follow ‘Laverne & Shirley’ actress dead at 88
 Eric Todisco Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:07 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Ronny Hallin, the sister of the late Garry and Penny Marshall, who produced and appeared in "Laverne & Shirley," has died. She was 88.
 Hallin's daughter, Penny, confirmed to Deadline that her mom "passed away peacefully at home" on Oct. 27.
 Born Jan. 2, 1938, in New York City, Hallin was the daughter of director and producer Anthony Masciarelli and tap dance teacher Marjorie Irene.
 Actress and producer Ronny Hallin died at age 88. Courtesy Penny Hallin
 Hallin was the sister of late Hollywood legends Garry and Penny Marshall. Gregory Pace / Shutterstock
 Her older brother, Garry, was famous for creating the shows "Laverne & Shirley," "Happy Days," "Mork & Mindy" and "The Odd Couple," and for directing the films "Pretty Woman," "The Princess Diaries," "Runaway Bride" and "Beaches."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Garry died in 2016 at age 81.
 Their sister, Penny, starred in "Laverne & Shirley" alongside Cindy Williams from 1976 to 1983, which earned her three Golden Globe nominations.
 Hallin appeared in and produced many of her brother Garry's projects, including "Laverne & Shirley." Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images
 Their sister Penny starred alongside Cindy Williams in "Laverne & Shirley." Getty Images
 She also directed "Jumpin' Jack Flash," "Big," "Awakenings," "A League of Their Own" and "Renaissance."
 Penny was first married to Michael Henry, with whom she welcomed daughter Tracy in 1964. Then, she was married to the late Rob Reiner , who adopted Tracy, from 1971 to 1981.
 Penny died in December 2018 at age 75.
 Penny was nominated for three Golden Globe Awards for "Laverne & Shirley." Getty Images
 Penny was married to the late Rob Reiner for ten years. Getty Images
 Advertisement Advertisement Hallin made her on-screen debut in a 1974 episode of her brother's ABC adaptation of "The Odd Couple."
 She worked with both her siblings on "Laverne & Shirley," producing the show and appearing in one episode as Maxine in 1982.
 Hallin also produced Garry's shows "Happy Days," "Blansky's Beauties," "Mork & Mindy," "Joanie Loves Chachi" and "Nothing in Common."
 Hallin worked with her siblings (all seen here in 2012) on numerous projects. FilmMagic
 Hallin produced "Happy Days," which her brother created. Courtesy Everett Collection
 As an actress, Hallin starred in the movies "Frankie and Johnny," "Exit to Eden" and "Raising Helen," all directed by her brother.
 Hallin had three children with her ex-husband, Larry Hallin.
 Larry died in February 2002 at age 69.
